name: Anath
overview: Anath is a male figure mentioned in the Book of Judges as the father of Shamgar. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe, lineage, or personal history. His mention is brief and serves primarily to identify Shamgar's ancestry.
namesAndTitles: The name Anath is a proper name that also corresponds to a Semitic goddess, though in this context it is used as a personal name rather than a divine title. The name itself was not given by God, indicating it may have cultural or regional origins outside direct divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Anath is the father of Shamgar, as noted in Judges 3:31. No other family relationships or descendants are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Anath's significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as the father of Shamgar, a judge of Israel mentioned briefly in Judges. Although Anath himself does not have a recorded role in Israel's deliverance or leadership, his mention establishes the lineage of Shamgar, who is recognized for his acts of deliverance. This connection highlights the importance of family lines in the biblical record, even when the individuals themselves are not extensively profiled.
